Class TtlBounds

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.substrate.core.ttl.TtlBounds
public final class TtlBounds extends Object
Shared TTL bound checks for the core primitive implementations.

Two distinct rules live here because substrate's TTL parameters fall into two groups.

Leases — an Atom's TTL, a Mailbox's TTL, and a Journal's inactivity TTL all answer "how long does this resource stay alive". A non-positive lease has no coherent meaning and backends disagree violently about what to do with one: Hazelcast's IMap reads 0 as infinite, the in-memory, PostgreSQL and MongoDB backends read it as already expired, DynamoDB writes no expiry attribute at all, Redis rejects EXPIRE key 0 outright, and NATS ignores the value. requirePositiveAtMost(String, Duration, Duration) rejects it up front so every backend agrees.

Retention hints — a Journal entry TTL and a Journal retention TTL are per-record hints rather than leases, and Duration.ZERO has an established meaning there: "store this without a TTL". The Cassandra, Redis, MongoDB and DynamoDB journal SPIs implement that for both entry and retention TTLs; Hazelcast implements it for the retention TTL only, since its append manages retention at the ringbuffer level and ignores the per-entry value entirely. Those parameters are not bounded from below by requireAtMost(String, Duration, Duration), which accepts zero but still rejects negatives.

One backend-specific nuance worth knowing: on Redis complete(Duration.ZERO) means "leave whatever TTL is already on the stream key in place" — the EXPIRE set by the last append still applies — rather than "retain forever".

    • requireAtMost

      public static void requireAtMost(String label, Duration ttl, Duration maxTtl)
      Validates a TTL against its upper bound, leaving Duration.ZERO legal but rejecting negative durations.

      A negative TTL has no meaning on any backend and none implements one deliberately — it is instead destructive. Redis reads a non-positive EXPIRE as "delete this key", so a negative entry TTL would wipe out the whole stream including every previously appended entry; Cassandra rejects USING TTL -1 with a query error, and MongoDB sweeps the document immediately.

      Parameters:
      label - the human-readable parameter name used in the exception message, e.g. "Journal entry TTL"
      ttl - the requested time-to-live
      maxTtl - the configured upper bound
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is negative or greater than maxTtl
